title: Definitional Sensitivity in Media Bias Detection: A Multi-Definition Dataset and Benchmark

bias_targets.methodology: Human and LLM annotators rated 300 news articles on a 6-point Likert scale using randomly assigned definitions of linguistic bias that varied in conceptual framing (biased word choice, grammatical agency manipulation, demeaning/stigmatizing labels) and length.

Human and LLM annotators rated 300 news articles on a 6-point Likert scale using randomly assigned definitions of gender bias that varied in conceptual framing (representational visibility, stereotypical trait attribution, irrelevant personal focus) and length.

Human and LLM annotators rated 300 news articles on a 6-point Likert scale using randomly assigned definitions of political bias that varied in conceptual framing (evaluative slant, selective issue coverage, interpretive framing) and length.

Human and LLM annotators rated 300 news articles on a 6-point Likert scale using randomly assigned definitions of text-level context bias that varied in conceptual framing (omission of relevant facts, asymmetric source treatment, gratuitous emotional detail) and length.
